MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 240, Ksh 160 and Ksh 350. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 760
   B. Ksh 750
   C. Ksh 850
   D. Ksh 650

2. 700 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 0.70
   B. Ksh 8
   C. Ksh 7
   D. Ksh 70

3. How many cents are in Ksh 8? (1 mark)
   A. 108 cents
   B. 8,000 cents
   C. 800 cents
   D. 80 cents

4. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 1,200, Ksh 2,350 and Ksh 875. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 4,435
   B. Ksh 4,325
   C. Ksh 4,425
   D. Ksh 4,525

5. One unit costs Ksh 45. What is the cost of 5 mandazi? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 235
   B. Ksh 180
   C. Ksh 225
   D. Ksh 50

6. Kip faces North and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. West
   C. East
   D. South

7. Kip faces South and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North
   C. West
   D. South

8. Kip faces North and makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South
   C. West
   D. North

9. A half turn makes (1 mark)
   A. a right angle
   B. a full turn
   C. a straight line
   D. a small angle

10. Which sign is used to mark a right angle in a drawing? (1 mark)
   A. A small triangle
   B. A small circle
   C. A small square in the corner
   D. A wavy line

11. What does the size of an angle depend on? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of the arms
   B. How far apart the arms are
   C. How long the arms are
   D. The number of arms

12. Which everyday object has a face that is a circle? (1 mark)
   A. A brick
   B. A roof end
   C. A coin
   D. A door

13. Which statement about a square is true? (1 mark)
   A. All four sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   B. It has only three corners
   C. It has no lines of symmetry
   D. Its opposite sides are different

14. How many lines of symmetry does a square have? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 1
   C. 2
   D. 4

15. What is the next shape in the pattern square, triangle, square, triangle, square, ...? (1 mark)
   A. Triangle
   B. Rectangle
   C. Square
   D. Circle

16. How many straight sides does a rectangle have? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 5
   C. 3
   D. 2

17. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many are walking or car together? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 9
   C. 6
   D. 8

18. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 10
   C. 11
   D. 12

19. Which is the safest way to count vehicles for a data project? (1 mark)
   A. Sitting on the road
   B. Standing in the middle of the road
   C. Running alongside the vehicles
   D. From a safe place inside the school gate with a teacher

20. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many more are there of walking than of bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 4

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Draw an angle using a ruler. Name the vertex and the arms and mark the angle with a small curve. (3 marks)

22. Mr Otieno has Ksh 2,000. He buys items costing Ksh 1,340. Does he have enough money? How much is left? (3 marks)

23. Explain what a right angle is. State how many right angles there are in (a) a rectangle, (b) a straight line, (c) a full turn. (5 marks)

24. A shopkeeper counts up to give change. A customer buys goods for Ksh 750 and pays with Ksh 1,000. Show how the shopkeeper counts up. (3 marks)

25. A sweet costs 50 cents. How many sweets can be bought with Ksh 10? (3 marks)

26. The raw data for 10 pupils' favourite fruits is: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. Make a tally table for this data. (4 marks)

27. Give two things you should do to stay safe when you collect data about vehicles. (2 marks)

28. Write instructions for a person to walk from the classroom door to the school gate using at least two turns. Use words such as forward, quarter turn, clockwise and anticlockwise. (4 marks)

29. A bicycle costs Ksh 6,500, a helmet Ksh 1,750 and a lock Ksh 850. Find the total cost. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Ksh 750
   Add the three costs: 240 + 160 + 350 = 750.

2. C — Ksh 7
   700 ÷ 100 = 7 remainder 0, so it is Ksh 7.

3. C — 800 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 8 = 8 × 100 = 800 cents.

4. C — Ksh 4,425
   Add the three costs: 1,200 + 2,350 + 875 = 4,425.

5. C — Ksh 225
   Cost = number × price = 5 × 45 = Ksh 225.

6. C — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives East.

7. C — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. South followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives West.

8. C — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a three-quarter turn clockwise gives West.

9. C — a straight line
   A half turn is two right angles, which form a straight line.

10. C — A small square in the corner
   A right angle is marked with a small square.

11. B — How far apart the arms are
   The size depends on the opening between the arms, not on their length.

12. C — A coin
   A coin is round and flat, so its face is a circle.

13. A — All four sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

14. D — 4
   A square can be folded down the middle both ways and along its two diagonals.

15. A — Triangle
   The pattern alternates between a square and a triangle, so a triangle comes next.

16. A — 4
   A rectangle has four straight sides.

17. A — 7
   6 + 1 = 7.

18. B — 10
   Add all the numbers: 6 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10.

19. D — From a safe place inside the school gate with a teacher
   Safety comes first. Count from a safe place and never stand in the road.

20. D — 4
   6 − 2 = 4.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with two straight lines meeting at a point, the point labelled vertex, the lines labelled arms and a curve between them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two straight arms, 1 mark for the vertex, 1 mark for the curve.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Yes. He has Ksh 660 left.
   Working / marking points: 2,000 is more than 1,340 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,340 (1 mark); Ksh 660 (1 mark).

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: A right angle is a square corner, made by a quarter turn. (a) 4 (b) 2 (c) 4
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for explaining a right angle (square corner or quarter turn), 1 mark for each of (a) 4, (b) 2 and (c) 4.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: From 750 to 800 is 50, and from 800 to 1,000 is 200. Change = 50 + 200 = Ksh 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for counting to 800, 1 mark for counting to 1,000, 1 mark for adding to make Ksh 250.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 sweets
   Working / marking points: Ksh 10 = 1,000 cents (1 mark); 1,000 ÷ 50 (1 mark); 20 sweets (1 mark).

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mango 4 (||||), banana 3 (|||), orange 2 (||), pawpaw 1 (|); total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count of two fruits (2 marks), 1 mark for correct tally marks, 1 mark for the total 10.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Count from a safe place inside the school gate and stay with a teacher. Do not stand in or near the road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible safety rule.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Walk forward 10 steps. Make a quarter turn clockwise. Walk forward 5 steps. Make a quarter turn anticlockwise. Walk to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first move with steps, 1 mark for a turn with its size, 1 mark for the turn direction, 1 mark for clear order.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 9,100
   Working / marking points: 6,500 + 1,750 = 8,250 (1 mark); 8,250 + 850 (1 mark); Ksh 9,100 (1 mark).
